day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight TP lands at 13:00, so no morning activities scheduled. Take the Aerobus or Metro (Red Line from Aeroporto) into the city centre for around €1.85–€2.00. Check in to Lisbon City Stay and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Baixa-Chiado neighbourhood on foot — a free and rewarding introduction to Lisbon. Stroll through Praça do Comércio along the Tagus waterfront, walk up Rua Augusta, and ride the historic Elevador de Santa Justa (€5.30 round trip) for panoramic rooftop views over the city.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Bairro Alto or Mouraria district for a relaxed first evening. Wander the hilly streets, soak in the atmosphere, and listen for live Fado music drifting from small tascas.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick pastel de nata (€1.20) and a bica (espresso, €0.80) at a local café near the hotel after check-in.
meals.lunch: Pick up a fresh bifana (pork sandwich) or prego roll from a local snack bar in Baixa for around €3–€4.
meals.dinner: Dine at a traditional tasca in Mouraria or Alfama — look for a prato do dia (dish of the day) which typically includes soup, main course, bread, and a drink for €8–€10. Try bacalhau à brás (shredded salt cod with eggs and potatoes).

day_by_day.notes: Buy a 24-hour Viva Viagem transport card (€0.50 card + top-up) at the airport Metro station — it pays off quickly. Keep your first evening light to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Tile Museum (Museu Nacional do Azulejo) — one of Lisbon's most unique and beautiful museums. Explore five centuries of Portuguese azulejo tile art housed in a stunning former convent. Entry is €5 (discounts available with Lisboa Card). Allow 2–2.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the historic Alfama district on foot — Lisbon's oldest neighbourhood. Climb to the Miradouro da Graça or Miradouro de Santa Luzia for sweeping city and river views (free). Browse the narrow cobblestone streets and visit the exterior of São Jorge Castle (entry €15, or admire it from outside to save budget).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Alfama for an authentic Fado experience. Many small restaurants offer free Fado with dinner — arrive early to secure a table. The music typically starts around 20:00–21:00.

meals.breakfast: Stop at a local pastelaria near the hotel — coffee and a pastel de nata or tosta mista (toasted ham and cheese) for under €3.
meals.lunch: Grab a meal at a neighbourhood restaurant near the Tile Museum — a prato do dia with soup, main, and drink for €8–€10. Try arroz de pato (duck rice) if available.
meals.dinner: Dine at a Fado tasca in Alfama — budget €12–€15 for a full meal including bread, olives, main course, and house wine. Avoid tourist-trap restaurants with large signs outside.

day_by_day.notes: The Tile Museum is closed on Mondays — Saturday is a great day to visit. Wear comfortable shoes; Alfama's cobblestones are steep and uneven. The Lisboa Card (1-day €22, 2-day €37) may be worth considering if you plan to visit multiple paid museums.

day_by_day.morning: Take Tram 15E or Bus 728 (included in transport card) to Belém — about 20–25 minutes from the city centre. Visit the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery, a breathtaking example of Manueline architecture (entry €10, or free on Sunday mornings before 14:00 — confirm current policy). Allow 1.5–2 hours inside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Belém Historical Quarter experience — walk along the riverside to the iconic Tower of Belém (entry €6). Browse the Padrão dos Descobrimentos (Monument to the Discoveries) exterior for free. Enjoy the riverside promenade and gardens at no cost.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to Chiado or Príncipe Real for the evening. Browse independent bookshops, boutiques, and enjoy the relaxed café culture of these charming neighbourhoods.

meals.breakfast: Stop at the world-famous Pastéis de Belém bakery (open since 1837) — the original pastéis de Belém cost around €1.40 each. Have 2–3 with a coffee for a classic Lisbon breakfast under €6.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from a local supermercado (supermarket) or grab takeaway from a café near Belém — sandwiches, fruit, and water for under €6. Eat in the riverside gardens.
meals.dinner: Try a cervejaria (beer hall/seafood restaurant) in Baixa or Cais do Sodré — grilled sardines (sardinhas grelhadas) or amêijoas à bulhão pato (clams) with bread and wine for €12–€15.

day_by_day.notes: Belém is a half-day destination easily combined with a leisurely afternoon. Sunday mornings can be busy at Jerónimos — arrive right when it opens. The pastéis at Pastéis de Belém are not to be missed — the recipe is a closely guarded secret.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Time Out Market Food Tour at Mercado da Ribeira in Cais do Sodré. Spend 2–3 hours sampling the best of Portuguese cuisine from top local chefs and producers — try petiscos (Portuguese tapas), fresh seafood, local cheeses, and regional wines. Budget €15–€20 for tasting multiple dishes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the LX Factory — a hip creative hub in a converted 19th-century industrial complex in Alcântara (free entry). Browse independent shops, street art, and galleries. On Mondays it is quieter than weekends, making it ideal for a relaxed visit. Afterwards, walk along the riverside to enjoy views of the 25 de Abril Bridge.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Cais do Sodré and Pink Street (Rua Nova do Carvalho) area for evening drinks and people-watching. This is Lisbon's nightlife hub — lively but accessible on a budget.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast near the hotel — galão (milky coffee) and a croissant or queijada for €2.50–€3.50.
meals.lunch: The Time Out Market visit covers your midday eating — graze on multiple small dishes across different stalls. A satisfying lunch of 3–4 items costs €12–€18.
meals.dinner: Try a tasca in Cais do Sodré or Santos neighbourhood — grilled chicken (frango assado) with rice and salad, or a hearty caldo verde soup with crusty bread for €8–€12.

day_by_day.notes: Time Out Market is busiest on weekends — Monday is a great time to visit without the crowds. LX Factory has a famous Sunday market, but the space is worth visiting any day of the week. Keep an eye out for happy hour deals at Cais do Sodré bars (typically 18:00–20:00).

day_by_day.morning: Take the scenic ferry from Cais do Sodré to Cacilhas across the Tagus River (€1.30 each way — one of the best budget experiences in Lisbon). Enjoy stunning views of the Lisbon skyline and the 25 de Abril Bridge. In Cacilhas, walk up to Cristo Rei statue (entry €6) for panoramic views of the entire city — a budget-friendly alternative to paid viewpoints.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lisbon by ferry and spend your last afternoon revisiting favourite neighbourhoods — perhaps Príncipe Real's antique market, the Miradouro do Parque Eduardo VII (free views), or last-minute souvenir shopping in Baixa. Pick up local products like ginjinha (cherry liqueur, €2–€3 a shot) or canned sardines as affordable gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in the Mouraria neighbourhood — the birthplace of Fado and one of Lisbon's most authentic areas. Enjoy a final Portuguese meal of grilled fish, petiscos, and local wine before packing for departure.

meals.breakfast: Last hotel-area café breakfast — pastel de nata, coffee, and fresh orange juice for €4–€5.
meals.lunch: In Cacilhas, try a local marisqueira (seafood restaurant) — grilled fish of the day with salad and bread for €10–€13, enjoyed with a river view.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on your last night — a full traditional dinner in Mouraria with soup, main course, dessert, and wine for €15–€18. Toast to a wonderful trip with a glass of vinho verde.

day_by_day.notes: The Cacilhas ferry is a highlight many tourists miss — highly recommended for the views alone. Check your flight details for Day 6 departure and arrange transport to the airport in advance (Metro Red Line is cheapest at ~€1.85). Pack any perishable food souvenirs carefully. Total estimated daily budget: €40–€60 per person including transport, entry fees, and meals.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Lisbon Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage, clear customs, and take the Aerobus or Metro (Red Line to Green Line) to central Lisbon. Check in to Lisbon City Stay, freshen up, and get oriented with a short stroll around the hotel neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Time Out Market (Mercado da Ribeira) for a self-guided introduction to Portuguese cuisine. Sample petiscos (Portuguese tapas), fresh seafood, pastel de bacalhau, and local wines from multiple vendors — a perfect first taste of Lisbon without committing to a sit-down meal after a long journey.
day_by_day.evening: Take a leisurely walk along the Ribeira waterfront promenade to shake off jet lag and enjoy the Tagus River views at golden hour. For dinner, head to a nearby traditional tasca in the Cais do Sodré or Bica neighborhood for a relaxed first evening meal.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a light snack at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Time Out Market — budget €15–20 per person sampling 3–4 stalls (bacalhau croquettes, grilled prawns, a glass of Vinho Verde)
meals.dinner: Taberna da Rua das Flores or similar traditional tasca — try caldo verde soup and grilled fish of the day; expect €20–28 per person with wine

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the 13:00 arrival. Validate a 24-hour or 48-hour Viva Viagem metro card at the airport for convenient transport throughout the trip. The Time Out Market is open until midnight so there's no rush.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a classic Lisbon breakfast at a local café — bica (espresso) and a torrada (thick buttered toast) or pastel de nata. Then head to the National Tile Museum (Museu Nacional do Azulejo) when it opens at 10:00. Spend 2–2.5 hours exploring five centuries of decorative azulejo tile art, including the stunning 18th-century panoramic panel of pre-earthquake Lisbon. The museum is housed in a former convent with a beautiful Baroque chapel.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the museum, take the tram or a short taxi to the Alfama District for the guided Alfama Walking Tour. Wind through medieval alleyways, visit the Miradouro da Graça or Portas do Sol viewpoint, and see the exterior of São Jorge Castle. The tour typically covers Alfama's Moorish origins, local life, and hidden squares.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Alfama for the Fado Show component of the tour (or book a standalone show at a respected casa de fado). Enjoy dinner paired with live Fado music — Portugal's soulful, UNESCO-recognized musical tradition. Many venues include a set dinner menu.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria Versailles or a local neighborhood café — pastel de nata + bica, €3–5
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the Tile Museum — try a bifanas (pork sandwich) or soup at a local café, €8–12
meals.dinner: Fado dinner at a casa de fado in Alfama (e.g., Mesa de Frades or Tasca do Chico) — set menu with wine, €35–45 per person; book in advance on Sundays

day_by_day.notes: The National Tile Museum is closed on Mondays, so Sunday is the ideal day to visit. Book the Fado show in advance as Sunday evenings fill up quickly. Wear comfortable shoes — Alfama's cobblestones are steep and uneven.

day_by_day.morning: Take Tram 28 (or Bus 727) westward to Belém for a full morning exploring the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery. Arrive early (opens 10:00) to beat crowds. Marvel at the intricate Manueline Gothic architecture, the double-cloistered courtyard, and the tombs of Vasco da Gama and Luís de Camões. Spend 1.5–2 hours here.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 10 minutes along the Tagus waterfront to the iconic Tower of Belém (Torre de Belém). Climb the tower for panoramic river views and admire its ornate Manueline stonework. Nearby, also visit the Monument to the Discoveries (Padrão dos Descobrimentos) for context on Portugal's Age of Exploration. Stop at the original Pastéis de Belém bakery (open since 1837) for the famous warm custard tarts dusted with cinnamon — a non-negotiable Lisbon experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Lisbon and explore the elegant Chiado and Bairro Alto neighborhoods. Browse independent bookshops (including the historic Livraria Bertrand), pop into the Santa Justa Lift viewpoint, and enjoy a relaxed dinner in Chiado.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a café near Lisbon City Stay, €5–8
meals.lunch: Pastéis de Belém bakery for custard tarts (€1.20 each) + a light snack, then a riverside café in Belém for grilled fish or a bifana, €12–18
meals.dinner: Tasca do Chico or Zé da Mouraria in Chiado/Bairro Alto — grilled sea bass or arroz de pato (duck rice), €22–30 per person with a glass of Alentejo red

day_by_day.notes: Belém is about 6 km west of central Lisbon — take Bus 727 from Praça do Comércio or Tram 15E from Praça da Figueira (approx. 20–30 min). Jerónimos Monastery is closed on Mondays in some seasons — verify hours in advance and adjust to Tower of Belém first if needed. Queue at Pastéis de Belém can be long; the takeaway line moves faster.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Mouraria, Lisbon's historic Moorish quarter and multicultural heart. Join the Traditional Tasca Lunch small-group experience that typically begins mid-morning with a neighborhood walk through Mouraria's narrow streets, visiting the Intendente square, street art murals, and local market stalls. Learn about the area's layered history — Moorish occupation, Jewish heritage, and immigrant communities.
day_by_day.afternoon: The Mouraria experience culminates in a traditional tasca lunch (included in the experience) featuring home-cooked Portuguese dishes like cozido à portuguesa (meat and vegetable stew), grilled sardines, or bacalhau à brás. After lunch, walk uphill to the Miradouro da Graça or Miradouro da Senhora do Monte for sweeping panoramic views of Lisbon's seven hills and the Tagus River — the best viewpoints in the city.
day_by_day.evening: Spend the evening in the lively Intendente or Anjos neighborhood — emerging creative districts with a mix of old-school tascas and contemporary wine bars. Visit a local mercearia (grocery-wine bar) for a Portuguese cheese and charcuterie board paired with natural wines from the Alentejo or Douro regions.

meals.breakfast: Café near Lisbon City Stay — galão (milky coffee) and a croissant or tosta mista, €4–6
meals.lunch: Included in the Traditional Tasca Lunch in Mouraria experience — hearty home-cooked Portuguese meal with wine, typically €25–35 per person
meals.dinner: Mercearia do Intendente or Taberna Albricoque — petiscos spread with local cheeses, presunto, olives, and natural wine; €18–25 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the Mouraria Tasca Lunch experience in advance as group sizes are small. Mouraria is easily walkable from most central Lisbon hotels. The miradouros (viewpoints) are free and best visited in late afternoon light. This is a great day to buy artisan souvenirs — look for handmade ceramics and azulejo tiles in Mouraria's small shops.

day_by_day.morning: Revisit any neighborhoods or sights you'd like to see again, or explore the elegant Príncipe Real district — known for its antique shops, garden square, and upscale food stores. Visit the Jardim do Príncipe Real for a quiet morning coffee under the giant cedar tree. Browse the weekend-style organic market (Mercado de Príncipe Real, open Saturdays but nearby shops open daily) and pick up local olive oils, wines, or preserves as gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praça do Comércio and the Baixa (downtown) area for a final leisurely walk along the Tagus waterfront. Visit the free viewpoint at Arco da Rua Augusta for rooftop views over the grand square and river. Pop into the Lisboa Story Centre for a quick multimedia overview of Lisbon's history including the 1755 earthquake. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping on Rua Augusta pedestrian street.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a well-regarded restaurant in Chiado or Bairro Alto — splurge slightly on a memorable final meal featuring the best of Portuguese cuisine. Consider a tasting menu or a classic bacalhau à Gomes de Sá (salt cod with potatoes and egg) paired with a bottle of Douro white wine. End the evening with a ginjinha (sour cherry liqueur) at a traditional ginjinha bar near Rossio square.

meals.breakfast: Café A Brasileira in Chiado (iconic literary café since 1905) — bica and pastel de nata, €5–7
meals.lunch: Cervejaria Ramiro-style seafood or a prego (steak sandwich) at Solar dos Presuntos — €15–22
meals.dinner: Alma or Tasca do Chico (Chiado) — farewell dinner with bacalhau or grilled black pork, full meal with wine €35–50 per person; reserve ahead

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if your departure flight is in the evening. The ginjinha at Ginjinha Sem Rival near Rossio is a beloved €1.50 local tradition — don't miss it. Consider buying a bottle of Ginjinha or a box of pastéis de nata from Pastéis de Belém (they travel well for a few hours) as edible souvenirs.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

day_by_day.afternoon: After check-in, take a leisurely stroll through the nearby Baixa-Chiado district. Explore the elegant Praça do Comércio waterfront square and the grand Rua Augusta Arch. Stop into a boutique for a light browse before heading toward the Chiado neighborhood's charming streets.
day_by_day.evening: Alfama District Walking Tour & Fado Show — Join an intimate guided walking tour through Lisbon's oldest medieval quarter as the golden hour light bathes the rooftops. Conclude the evening at an authentic, upscale Fado house for a soul-stirring live performance paired with Portuguese wine.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or at airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Light welcome lunch at the hotel restaurant or a nearby upscale café such as Café A Brasileira in Chiado — try a Francesinha or prawn croquettes with a glass of Vinho Verde.
meals.dinner: Dinner included as part of the Fado Show experience at a premium Fado house such as Clube de Fado or Sr. Fado — expect traditional petiscos, bacalhau, and fine Douro reds.

day_by_day.notes: Private airport transfer recommended for a seamless luxury arrival. Confirm Fado Show reservation in advance as top venues book quickly. Comfortable walking shoes advised for cobblestone streets.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the hotel followed by a visit to the National Tile Museum (Museu Nacional do Azulejo). Enjoy a private or small-group guided tour through five centuries of Portugal's iconic azulejo tile art, including the stunning 18th-century panoramic tile panel of pre-earthquake Lisbon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Traditional Tasca Lunch in Mouraria — Explore Lisbon's historic Moorish quarter on a small-group culinary walk. Sample authentic petiscos, smoked sausages, local cheeses, and regional wines in intimate family-run tascas tucked into the neighborhood's winding lanes.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a relaxed evening. Enjoy cocktails at the hotel bar or rooftop terrace if available, followed by a reservation at one of Lisbon's Michelin-starred restaurants for a refined tasting menu.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the hotel — fresh pastries, smoked ham, local cheeses, fruit, and freshly brewed coffee.
meals.lunch: Included in the Traditional Tasca Lunch in Mouraria experience — multiple tastings of authentic Portuguese small plates and regional wines.
meals.dinner: Tasting menu dinner at Alma (Chef Henrique Sá Pessoa, Michelin-starred) in Chiado — contemporary Portuguese cuisine with exceptional wine pairing.

day_by_day.notes: The National Tile Museum is a short taxi or Uber ride from the city center. Book Michelin-starred dinner reservation well in advance. The Mouraria food tour is best enjoyed with an empty stomach.

day_by_day.morning: Private half-day excursion to Belém Historical Quarter. Visit the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery, a breathtaking example of Manueline Gothic architecture, followed by a tour of the iconic Tower of Belém on the Tagus riverbank. Optionally visit the Monument to the Discoveries for panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at the legendary Pastéis de Belém bakery for the world-famous original custard tarts (pastéis de nata), dusted with cinnamon — a true Lisbon institution since 1837. Afterward, visit the nearby Berardo Collection Museum for a dose of modern and contemporary art before heading back to the city center.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a premium miradouro (viewpoint) such as Miradouro de Santa Catarina or a rooftop bar like TOPO Chiado, followed by an elegant dinner in the Príncipe Real neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — opt for a light spread before the morning excursion.
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic-style lunch or a sit-down meal at Feitoria restaurant in Belém — one of Lisbon's finest waterfront dining experiences with a Michelin star and views over the Tagus.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tasca do Chico or Taberna da Rua das Flores in Príncipe Real — intimate, upscale Portuguese tavern cuisine featuring seasonal ingredients and natural wines.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private car or premium taxi for the Belém trip (~6 km from city center) for comfort. Jerónimos Monastery can be crowded on weekends — arrive early or book a priority-access tour. The pastéis queue moves quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Time Out Market Food Tour — Spend a curated morning at Lisbon's iconic Time Out Market in Cais do Sodré. Join a guided tasting session sampling signature dishes from the market's top-rated chefs and producers, including fresh seafood, artisan cheeses, charcuterie, and Portuguese wines.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the LX Factory, a creative hub set in a 19th-century industrial complex nearby. Browse designer boutiques, art galleries, and independent bookshops. Alternatively, visit the Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga (National Museum of Ancient Art) for an immersive journey through Portuguese and European masterpieces.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset river cruise on the Tagus with canapés and sparkling wine, offering spectacular views of the 25 de Abril Bridge and Lisbon's skyline. Return to shore for a late dinner at a premium seafood restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel or a neighborhood pastelaria — coffee, croissant, and fresh orange juice.
meals.lunch: Included in the Time Out Market Food Tour — curated multi-vendor tasting experience.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cervejaria Ramiro — Lisbon's legendary premium seafood brasserie. Order tiger prawns, percebes (barnacles), lobster, and cold Sagres beer or a crisp Alentejo white.

day_by_day.notes: Book the private sunset Tagus cruise in advance through the hotel concierge. Time Out Market tours are best on weekdays when slightly less crowded. Cervejaria Ramiro may have a wait — reservations strongly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed final morning — sleep in and enjoy a long, indulgent hotel breakfast. Optionally visit the Museu Calouste Gulbenkian, one of Europe's finest private art collections, featuring Egyptian antiquities, Islamic art, Impressionist paintings, and stunning sculpture gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute luxury shopping in the Chiado district — visit concept stores, Portuguese leather goods shops, and artisan ceramic boutiques for premium souvenirs. Stop for a final bica (espresso) and pastel de nata at a classic Lisbon café.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at an iconic Lisbon restaurant — celebrate the final evening with a grand meal before departure preparations.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent hotel breakfast — full spread with champagne or fresh juice, smoked salmon, pastries, and local specialties.
meals.lunch: Elegant lunch at Bairro do Avillez (Chef José Avillez) in Chiado — a refined yet relaxed multi-concept restaurant celebrating the best of contemporary Portuguese cuisine.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Belcanto (Chef José Avillez, two Michelin stars) — Lisbon's most celebrated fine dining destination, offering a transcendent tasting menu rooted in Portuguese culinary heritage with world-class technique and presentation.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure logistics with the hotel concierge — arrange a private transfer for your outbound flight. Belcanto requires reservations weeks in advance; book before the trip begins. Pack any ceramic, wine, or food purchases carefully to bring home.
